correctness.rationale: Upper bounds are obtained for every real p-Banach target by extending to any leaf image (constant 2) and to the arithmetic barycenter (constant 2^{1+1/p}/3) via the p-triangle inequality. In canonical free p-space over the side-two equilateral triple, the source provides exact three-spanning-tree norm formula, referenced to Cúth–Raunig Thm 2.2/Cor 2.7. Contractive comparison to the ordinary free Banach norm rules out centers with any negative barycentric coefficient for a minimizing radius ≤2. On simplex coordinates (a,b,c), sorted a≤b≤c, the maximum of three distances is 2(b^p+c^p)^{1/p}; strict concavity over the ordered simplex for 0<p<1 drives minima to the leaf vertices or the uniform barycenter. At p=1 the minimizing smallest coefficient enforces unique barycenter. Exact threshold 3^p=2 gives log2/log3, with precisely the three leaves and barycenter as minimizers at transition. Canonical embedding realizes Lipschitz constant one and gives universal sharpness. The actual verification/check.py subtree and blob were inspected: finite 4,960-point grids and p1 rational grid are diagnostic only, not proof for continuous p/all targets.

Bíma 2402.03189 Theorem 30 uses the collinear trace N={0,1,2} and an added point 3/2, unlike equilateral leaves/star midpoint; its Banach endpoint trace 1 differs from our 4/3. Resultary also contains later separate SCOPE n≥4 star formula min(2,2(n−1)^{1/p}/n), explicitly scoped to n≥4 and crediting pre-existing n=3. The n≥4 mathematical proof can be algebraically adapted to n=3 but its stated theorem excludes this case, and neither that extension nor simple matching symbols is an earlier general published theorem covering n=3. value.rationale: Sharp universal extension constants into all real quasi-Banach p-targets for the smallest genuinely branching star provide a motivated exact benchmark, with the substantive discontinuous switch of all optimal free-space center images at p=log2/log3.
